identity.spin_note: Four I=1/2 protons give a spin product 2^4=16. Divide spectroscopic Q by 16 to compare with nuclear-spin-free thermochemistry in the high-temperature equilibrium convention. Td state weights 5,5,2,3,3 are already included. Do not additionally divide by rotational symmetry 12 or confuse the HITRAN state-independent gi=1 with the complete spin product. No isotope-resolved equilibrium is modeled.

printed_janaf.evaluation: March 1961; current table converted to 1 bar
printed_janaf.uncertainty_definition: Not separately recovered; do not interpret as 95% limits or propagate independently.
thermal_ancestry: Stevenson and Ibers (1960): bond distance and force constants
printed_janaf.energy_ancestry: Rossini (1931) combustion, recomputed with then-accepted formation enthalpies of water and CO2.

atct.uncertainty_definition: Estimated 95% confidence limits; correlated network, not propagated as independent errors.
atct.independence_note: ATcT combines calorimetry, equilibrium and theory. Thermal functions enter third-law reductions; the energy evaluation does not independently validate the full high-temperature thermal curve.

wenger2008.method: Fitted lower polyads plus statistical rotational and Morse extrapolation of high polyads toward dissociation
wenger2008.uncertainty_note: At 300 and 1000 K the reported value is less than 0.1%, represented here as an upper bound. These are model-based estimates, not specified confidence intervals. Nikitin (2015) later questions the high-energy statistical approximation; retain this as a historical diagnostic, not a preferred benchmark.

mm2024.note: Calculated energies are replaced by MARVEL energies where available. The downloaded file extends to 5000 K, but the published completeness estimate is 2000 K. No all-state caloric validation to 4000 K is established.

followups: Reconcile CH4 TIPS2021 and TIPS2025 arrays against versioned original datasets and generators; investigate truncation, models and publication/file differences without assuming their cause.
Read Nikitin (2015) and its 2017 corrected Table 4, including convergence to 3000 K. Do not use the insufficiently precise original fitted coefficients.
Obtain bound-state and near-dissociation coverage with first and second energy moments through 4000 K, using common isotope and spin conventions.
Then choose a continuous G/H/S/Cp model and evaluate a finite equilibrium substitution.
decision: Retain the existing JANAF molecular thermal functions, NASA atomic thermal functions and balanced ATcT energy operationally. Neither raw NASA nor a wholesale MM/TIPS replacement is justified over 1500-4000 K. The physical accuracy of the existing thermal model remains unknown.
